title: Continuous capture exceeds functional needs
description: Wearing the device causes continuous capture of sensor telemetry (heart rate, step counts, GPS position, timestamps), processing personal data more frequently than may be functionally necessary.

title: Sensitive data types collected
description: Heart rate (health/biometric) and GPS position (location) are sensitive personal data captured continuously by the wearable device.

title: Quasi-identifiers enable identification
description: GPS position combined with timestamps in the telemetry data can serve as quasi-identifiers to identify the data subject.

title: Device ID enables linking of sync data to specific wearable
description: The wearable device shares a unique device identifier along with sensor batches (exercise sessions, GPS traces, timestamps), allowing the data to be linked to a particular device and thus its owner across syncs.
assumptions: Device ID is unique per device and persistent.

title: Identified metadata in transit during sync
description: Metadata of the communication flow (e.g., device ID, timestamps) contains identified information that can reveal the data subject's identity during transmission from wearable to app.
assumptions: Device ID is transmitted in clear or as part of protocol metadata.

title: Sensitive GPS location data received by companion app
description: The companion app receives highly sensitive GPS traces and exercise data which may not be strictly necessary for all app functions, increasing disclosure risk at the destination.
assumptions: GPS data is considered sensitive personal data under typical privacy contexts.

title: Excessive sensor batch volume synced from device
description: Batches of sensor data including detailed GPS traces and timestamps are synced in volume that may exceed minimal functional needs for basic exercise tracking.
assumptions: Detailed traces are not always required; aggregated summaries could suffice for some features.

title: User unaware of detailed data processing in companion app
description: Data subject may be unaware of the full scope of processing (storage, analysis) of GPS traces and sessions once received by the mobile app.
assumptions: App UI or notices do not fully inform users of data handling.
uncertainty_note: Based on typical app behaviors; no specific UI details given.

title: Sharing of sensitive health data
description: The user shares calorie intake, meals, and weight entries, which constitute sensitive personal health data, with the companion app.

title: Collection of sensitive health data
description: The companion app receives and processes sensitive health data including calorie intake, meals, and weight entries from the user.

title: Processing of identified health data
description: The app processes the logged data in the context of the known user/wearer account, making it identified personal data.

title: Attributable health data records
description: Logged calorie, meal, and weight entries create data records that can be attributed to the specific user, preventing denial of the logged information.

title: Storage of sensitive health data types
description: The Health Log Store receives and persists highly sensitive personal health information including calorie intake, weight history, and exercise sessions, which exceeds typical sensitivity levels and requires strict necessity justification.
uncertainty_note: Flow description provides no details on whether this data is strictly required for core functionality or if minimization was applied.

title: Propagation of health logs during write
description: Personal health data is transmitted over the data flow to the store, making it accessible during transit to any intermediaries or in case of interception.
uncertainty_note: No information given on encryption or protection of the data flow.

title: User unawareness of health log storage
description: The Companion Mobile App shares detailed health logs without explicit indication that users are fully informed about the storage destination and implications.
uncertainty_note: Flow description lacks any detail on consent or notice mechanisms at the time of writing the logs.

title: Location traces as quasi-identifiers
description: GPS location traces with timestamps stored in the location history can serve as quasi-identifiers to link data to specific individuals through unique movement patterns.

title: Quasi-identifying location history
description: The data store receives and holds location traces that contain combinations of attributes (positions + timestamps) unique to a data subject, enabling identification.

title: Location data as attributable evidence
description: Stored GPS traces with timestamps provide data evidence that can attribute presence or actions to an individual, preventing denial of claims about location at specific times.

title: Sensitive location data written to store
description: The app writes highly sensitive GPS location data, which depending on context may exceed strict functional necessity or introduce disclosure risks at the point of sharing.

title: Profiling an individual through health data analysis
description: The Health Analytics Service analyzes calorie, weight, and exercise logs across sessions for health-condition analysis, which involves profiling individuals based on patterns in their personal health data.

title: Processing of sensitive health data types
description: The analytics service reads and processes sensitive personal data types including calorie, weight, and exercise logs, which are highly sensitive and require strict necessity justification.

title: Profiling an individual from location history
description: Analytics service queries and analyzes location history across sessions to derive daily routine and movement patterns, linking data to the individual through behavioral profiling.

title: Distinguishable individual via unique movement patterns
description: Location history and derived movement patterns allow singling out the data subject as their routines are likely unique, making the anonymity set too small.

title: Processing of sensitive location data
description: The destination processes highly sensitive location history data to derive routines, which may exceed strict functional necessity or introduce unnecessary sensitivity risks.

title: Sharing of sensitive health risk indicators
description: Health Analytics Service returns health-condition risk indicators, routine summaries and trend flags which constitute highly sensitive personal health data.

title: Profiling-based linking via returned insights
description: Inferred insights about health conditions enable linking of data to an individual through analysis of patterns and derived health profiles.

title: Receipt of sensitive inferred health data
description: Companion Mobile App receives health risk indicators and trend flags, exposing the app (and potentially its storage or display) to sensitive personal data.

title: Profiling via inferred health risk signals
description: The app performs analysis to infer eating-disorder or diabetes risk indicators from user data and displays these trends, linking patterns back to the individual wearer.

title: Disclosure of sensitive inferred health data
description: Highly sensitive condition indicators (eating disorder or diabetes risk signals) are processed and shown on the dashboard, exceeding minimal functional needs for a companion app.

title: Unnecessary analysis and inference on personal data
description: Personal data is analyzed and enriched through inference to produce condition risk signals, which is not strictly required for basic trend display functionality.

title: Unawareness of inference processing
description: The wearer may remain unaware of the full scope of data collection, profiling, and inference that leads to the displayed risk indicators.

title: Disclosure of sensitive health and location data to third-party cloud
description: The full health and location dataset along with analytics data and models is hosted and replicated at the third-party cloud provider, disclosing highly sensitive personal data types beyond what may be strictly necessary for basic hosting.

title: Data subjects unaware of third-party hosting and replication
description: The Health Analytics Service shares the complete dataset with an external cloud provider for hosting without mechanisms ensuring data subjects are informed about this processing and storage location.

title: Risk of unlawful processing of special category health data
description: Storing and replicating the full health and location dataset at a third-party provider may constitute unlawful processing under regulations like GDPR if appropriate safeguards, consent, or legal basis for third-party involvement are not in place.
